<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
b.a1e9343464:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.

De libro Ecclesiástici
<r>Sir 3:27-30</r>
<n>27</n> Cor durum habébit male in novíssimo, et qui amat perículum in illo períbit.
<n>28</n> Cor ingrédiens duas vias non habébit succéssus, et pravus corde in illis scandalizábitur.
<n>29</n> Cor nequam gravábitur in dolóribus, et peccátor adíciet ad peccándum.
<n>30</n> Synagógæ superbórum non erit sánitas, frutex enim peccáti radicábitur in illis, et non intellégitur.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Ante omnes colles generávit me Dóminus.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Ecclesiasticus
<r>Sir 3:27-30</r>
<n>27</n> A hard heart shall fear evil at the last: and he that loveth danger shall perish in it.
<n>28</n> A heart that goeth two ways shall not have success, and the perverse of heart shall be scandalized therein.
<n>29</n> A wicked heart shall be laden with sorrows, and the sinner will add sin to sin.
<n>30</n> The congregation of the proud shall not be healed: for the plant of wickedness shall take root in them, and it shall not be perceived.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> God possessed me in the beginning, before He made the earth, before He created the depths, before He caused the fountains of water to spring.before the mountains were settled, before there were any hills, did the Lord beget me.

* Before the mountains were settled, before there were any hills, did the Lord beget me.

<n>33</n> Ignem ardéntem exstínguit aqua, et eleemósyna resístit peccátis;
<n>34</n> Et Deus prospéctor est eius qui reddit grátiam, méminit eius in pósterum, et in témpore casus sui invéniet firmaméntum.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>exto Kaléndas Septémbris Luna vicésima quinta. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>S</h>ancti Ioséphi Calasánctii, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui Ordinis Clericórum Regulárium Páuperum Matris Dei Scholárum Piárum éxstitit Fundátor, atque octávo Kaléndas Septémbris obdormívit in Dómino.
<h>P</h>oténtiæ, in Lucánia, pássio sanctórum Aróntii, Honoráti, Fortunáti et Sabiniáni; qui, sanctórum Bonifátii et Theclæ fílii, a Valeriáno Iúdice, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre, iussi sunt capitálem subíre senténtiam. Eórum tamen ac reliquórum ex duódecim frátribus festum Kaléndis Septémbris celebrátur.
<h>B</h>érgomi sancti Narni, qui, a beáto Bárnaba baptizátus, primus ab ipso eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopus ordinátus est.
<h>C</h>ápuæ natális sancti Rufi, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, cum esset patríciæ dignitátis, a beáto Apollináre, sancti Petri discípulo, cum univérsa família baptizátus est.
<h>I</h>bídem sanctórum Mártyrum Rufi et Carpóphori, qui sub Diocletiáno et Maximiáno passi sunt.
<h>T</h>omis, in Ponto, sanctórum Mártyrum Marcellíni Tribúni, et uxóris Mannéæ, ac filiórum Ioánnis, Serapiónis et Petri.
<h>A</h>pud Leontínos, in Sicília, sanctæ Euthalíæ Vírginis, quæ, cum esset Christiána, ad cæléstem Sponsum, a fratre suo Sermiliáno cæsa gládio, migrávit.
<h>E</h>ódem die pássio sanctæ Anthúsæ iunióris, quæ ob Christi fidem, in púteum mersa, martýrium sumpsit.
<h>A</h>reláte, in Gállia, sancti Cæsárii Epíscopi, miræ sanctitátis et pietátis viri.
<h>A</h>ugustodúni sancti Syágrii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>P</h>apíæ sancti Ioánnis Epíscopi.
<h>I</h>lérdæ, in Hispánia Tarraconénsi, sancti Licérii Epíscopi.
<h>I</h>n Thebáide sancti Póemenis Anachorétæ.
<h>A</h>pud Septempedános, in Picéno, sanctæ Margarítæ Víduæ.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.a0299b4ee6:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>ugust 27th 2027, the 25th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Bergamo, [about the year 75,] holy Narnus, who was baptized by blessed Barnabas, and was ordained by him to be the first Bishop of that city.
<h>A</h>t Capua, [towards the end of the first century,] the holy martyr Rufus, Bishop [of that see.] A man of Patrician family, who was baptized along with all his house by blessed Apollinaris, the disciple of holy Peter.
<h>L</h>ikewise at Capua, the holy martyrs Rufus and Carpophorus, who suffered under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian.
<h>A</h>t Tomi, [about the year 303,] in Pontus, the holy martyrs Marcellinus the Tribune, Mannea his wife, and their sons, John, Serapion, and Peter.
<h>A</h>t Lentini, in Sicily, [about the year 256,] the holy Virgin Euthalia, who was slain by her own brother Sermilian with the sword, because she was a Christian, and so passed away to Christ the Bridegroom.
<h>O</h>n the same day holy Anthusa the younger received martyrdom by being drowned in a well for Christ's faith's sake.
<h>A</h>t Arles, [in the year 542,] holy Caesarius, Bishop of that city, a man of marvellous holiness and godliness.
<h>A</h>t Autun, [about the year 600,] the holy Confessor Syagrius, Bishop [of that see.]
<h>A</h>t Pavia, [in the year 813,] holy John, Bishop [of that see.]
<h>A</h>t Lerida, in Spain, holy Licerius, Bishop [of that see.]
<h>I</h>n the Thebaid, [about the year 450,] the holy Hermit Poemon [or Pastor, Abbot of Scete.]
<h>A</h>t San Severino, in the March of Ancona, [in the year 1396,] the holy widow Margaret.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
